body:
I created a new Godot **4.5-stable** project using the same nodes, scripts, custom icon and settings as the MRP in my initial post, exported it to Android, and it does **not** use the custom icon.

I observed this icon issue on a large project, which I'll call F,  that I started in August 2023, using whatever Godot version was current at that time, probably 4.0.4. Since then, I've been upgrading the project to new Godot versions when they were published.

Before I upgraded the exported F project from 4.5-stable to 4.6-dev1, the custom icon **was** used. So now I'm confused.

This regression is most likely caused by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/110566
That PR updates the source assets to use WebP format but does not update the export logic in `export_plugin.cpp`, which still assumes the assets are in PNG format and is specifically implemented to handle PNGs.
CC @Alex2782 @lumiscosity
Oh, I only grepped for usages within the resources subfolder since Android file schemas are filetype-agnostic... I'll make a PR to fix this in a second.
I tried poking at it a bit but I was unable to get it working. Would need some help with this...

@Alex2782 The icon paths are hardcoded in `export_plugin.cpp` file, it's used to search and replace icons in template. These searches would now fail because file extenstion is now changed to `.webp` but logic still searches for `.png` https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d413181b8a6c427a56d6c37378d4dec8e658b630/platform/android/export/export_plugin.cpp#L3991

There's many similar logic in this file that needs to be updated to work with both webp and png files.
I see that Windows and MacOs export support more image formats, we should standardize this.

@Alex2782 Have you tested with the gradle build? I think it would cause issues with gradle build because here https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/d413181b8a6c427a56d6c37378d4dec8e658b630/platform/android/export/export_plugin.cpp#L1944-L1950 in ths part, png data would be stored in a file with `.webp` extension.

> in ths part, png data would be stored in a file with `.webp` extension. Yes, this is what the files in the APK files look like (with and without a Gradle build). It doesn't seem to be a problem. _(Samsung Tab S7, Android 13)_ Android probably checks the content to determine the file type. We should still convert it properly and include more formats, like when exporting for Windows or macOS. I'll take another look at it in the next few days. If it's too complex, it could take me several weeks; right now, I don't have much time.
